description: Somos un grupo de estudiantes de la escuela Epa n°2 Puertas del sol interesados en ganar y aprender más sobre la astronomia.
summary: Hello, we are SECTOR 404, a group of 7 members from San Luis, Argentina, participating in the "Space Mission Game" challenge. We have incorporated the MDL (Mission Design Laboratory) tool into one of our missions. We are students between the ages of 12 and 14, and through this game, we hope to spark interest among our peers and help them learn more about space missions—covering everything from mechanics and rocket selection to orbital dynamics. In our game, there are four main characters; depending on the player's choices, they will travel to either the Moon or Mars to complete specific objectives. Throughout the game, players must tackle various tasks and mini-games to progress through all 5 levels. In short, our goal is to foster knowledge of and interest in astronomical and space-related activities among young people and teenagers. Thank you.
details: SECTOR 404 is an interactive, gamified educational platform built as an immersive first-person web environment whose purpose is to comprehensively simulate the design, planning, and execution cycle of a space mission to the Moon or Mars through three dynamic phases consisting of a preparation and selection phase where the user chooses a destination and specialized crew, an engineering and assembly phase where the user interacts with a technical decision-making panel based on orbital physics, weight, and payload where incorrect calculations trigger critical failure and correct ones pass the launch test, and an in-route navigation phase where the spacecraft overcomes real-time challenges like micrometeoroid storms or compression warnings to test operational resilience, offering benefits such as immersive STEAM education that transforms complex astrophysics and aerospace engineering into active gamified learning, critical thinking and problem-solving that compels users to understand cause-and-effect relationships between physics and technical viability, and cross-platform accessibility designed for smooth performance on desktop and mobile devices without specialized hardware, with an anticipated impact focused on sparking scientific and technological vocations among students, breaking down the barrier that space exploration is inaccessible, and equipping classrooms with an autonomous interactive resource that fosters digital literacy and inquiry-based learning, developed using a tech stack comprising HTML5, advanced CSS3 with glassmorphism effects, and modern JavaScript for the web environment, Canvas API and WebGL for graphics and rendering, and frontend development environments with code-assistance platforms for a self-contained modular architecture, demonstrating creativity through its ability to blend interactive science fiction storytelling with real aerospace engineering principles where spacecraft design has immediate logical consequences to turn errors into powerful pedagogical tools for trial and continuous improvement alongside a clean futuristic aesthetic and touch adaptability, while taking into account design and feasibility factors such as usability and accessibility prioritizing an intuitive interface with dark tones and neon accents to reduce eye strain, technical performance optimized as a lightweight system for modern web browsers without complex installations, and narrative and scientific consistency balancing technical rigor with an engaging, playful approach.
